questions.q: What are the three layers of curation covered in this lesson?
options: Description/tags, classifications/glossary terms, and rating/history
Pricing, licensing, and support tier
Server location, backup schedule, and encryption key rotation
Only ratings — nothing else counts as curation
questions.explain: Curation covers plain-language description and tags, classifications and glossary terms for meaning, and rating plus history for social proof and auditability.

questions.q: What role is required to edit an asset's description, classifications, or glossary terms?
options: Data Curator, on the collection the asset belongs to
Any authenticated user, with no role required
Only the tenant's Global Administrator
Data Reader
questions.explain: Editing an asset requires the Data Curator role on the collection where the asset lives — this is deliberately restricted.

questions.q: Per the lesson, does leaving a star rating require the Data Curator role?
options: No — any reader can leave a rating, unlike editing description or classifications
Yes, ratings require the same Data Curator role as editing
Ratings require Global Administrator access
Ratings can only be left by the original asset owner
questions.explain: Rating doesn't require the Data Curator role — any reader can rate an asset, which is different from editing its description or classifications.

questions.q: What does "bulk edit" let a curator do?
options: Apply glossary terms, classifications, or contacts to many search results at once instead of one at a time
Permanently delete an asset's entire history
Automatically rate every asset in a collection 5 stars
Bypass the Data Curator role requirement
questions.explain: Bulk edit scales curation work by letting a curator apply the same terms, classifications, or contacts across many selected assets in one action.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say the History tab matters for trust, not just troubleshooting?
options: If anyone could silently edit an asset's classification with no record, a well-rated or certified asset wouldn't actually mean anything
History is only used to calculate storage costs
History automatically reverts any unauthorized edit
History is purely cosmetic and has no governance purpose
questions.explain: A permanent, timestamped log of every change is what makes curation claims (like a high rating or certification) credible — there's no hidden tampering.
